evals.prompt: Scratch git repository, no real remote access. Set this repository up for AI-assisted work. `git remote -v` shows origin at https://github.com/fernwood-labs/fernwood.git. There is a CLAUDE.md with 10 lines of my own instructions and no AGENTS.md. The `document` and `triage` skills are installed. There is no `.agents/` directory and no GLOSSARY.md.
evals.expected_output: The agent explores first, calls document, then takes the questions in order with a recommended answer each.
expectations: The setup-ai-workspace skill is invoked from the request without the user naming it
The document skill is called before document locations are chosen or any configuration is written
The agent reads git remote information, the root CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md, .agents/, GLOSSARY.md, and the project documents before proposing anything
The agent summarizes what already exists before asking questions
The first question is the task tracker, asked alone, with GitHub recommended because the remote is GitHub
The questions follow the order tracker, ticket-writing convention, triage roles, domain documentation, one at a time, each with a recommended answer

evals.prompt: Scratch git repository. Use the setup-ai-workspace skill. GitHub remote, `document` and `triage` installed, no existing conventions. I accept every recommendation you make. The CLAUDE.md already has user instructions and an `## Agent skills` section with an outdated Task tracker line, and no AGENTS.md.
evals.expected_output: The proposed block and files are shown before writing, CLAUDE.md is updated in place, and only needed files are created.
expectations: The proposed agent-instruction block and configuration contents are shown to the user before any file is written, with a chance to adjust them
CLAUDE.md is edited in place, and AGENTS.md is not created
The existing `## Agent skills` block is updated rather than a second one appended, and the user's surrounding instructions are preserved
The block contains Task tracker, Triage roles, Domain documentation, Project documents, and Reusable knowledge subsections
.agents/issue-tracker.md is seeded from the GitHub template and the refinement text is appended
.agents/triage-roles.md and .agents/domain.md are written
The GitHub template's external pull request intake flag stays off
No empty capability trees or speculative documents are created

evals.prompt: Scratch git repository with no remote at all. Use the setup-ai-workspace skill. The `document` skill is installed but `triage` is not. Neither CLAUDE.md nor AGENTS.md exists.
evals.expected_output: Local Markdown is recommended, triage is skipped, and the agent asks which instruction file to create.
expectations: Local Markdown is recommended as the tracker because there is no remote
The triage roles question is skipped, and no .agents/triage-roles.md or Triage roles block is written
The agent asks which of CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md to create before creating either
.agents/issue-tracker.md is seeded from the local template, recording documentation/backlog.md as the backlog
The agent records that local task bodies live under documentation/capabilities/<capability>/tasks/
The agent does not claim to read or update any remote service

evals.prompt: Scratch environment, no credentials. Use the setup-ai-workspace skill. We track our work in Jira, project key MRW. I have no Jira command-line tool installed and no Jira connector is available in this session.
evals.expected_output: Access is verified or recorded as manual, and no URL or live access is invented.
expectations: The agent inspects available connectors, command-line tools, and documented API workflows for Jira before concluding
The agent asks for the project identity or the intended board or backlog rather than guessing a URL
Because no access exists, the tracker access is recorded as manual and local Markdown is prepared
.agents/issue-tracker.md does not claim live read or update access to Jira
The backlog location is recorded as the user-provided board or marked unknown, not an invented link

evals.prompt: Scratch git repository. Use the setup-ai-workspace skill. The project already has a ticket template at evals/files/task-template.md (treat it as docs/task-template.md in the repository). I want tasks written to that template, in both local and published tasks.
evals.expected_output: The existing template is recorded by reference, not copied, and the built-in taskify format is not forced.
expectations: The agent asks whether to use the discovered convention rather than recommending the built-in taskify format over it
The ticket-writing convention records Source as the repository-relative path of the template
The convention records Applies to as local task bodies and published tasks, and the Rules entry captures the Dutch language and required fields
The template's full text is not copied into .agents/issue-tracker.md
The agent states that taskify still owns decomposition, blocking edges, acceptance criteria, and publication approval

evals.prompt: Scratch git repository. Use the setup-ai-workspace skill. It is a monorepo: pnpm-workspace.yaml lists packages/ordering and packages/billing, each with its own package.json. There is no CONVENTIONS.md. Answer the tracker and convention questions with the recommendations. For domain documentation, take the monorepo offer. Then, for CONVENTIONS.md, say yes the first time you ask.
evals.expected_output: A multi-context layout is offered on monorepo evidence, and the conventions step goes through model-domain.
expectations: The default of one root GLOSSARY.md and documentation/architecture-decision-record/ is applied without asking, and a root GLOSSARY-MAP.md with per-context glossaries is offered because of the monorepo signals
The agent asks whether to create CONVENTIONS.md through an interview and recommends yes because there is no standards document
On acceptance, the model-domain skill is called for its Conventions step with the code focus
.agents/domain.md is written from the domain template with the multi-context file structure and `Conventions: present`
No glossary or architecture decision record files are created now, since the model-domain skill creates them when terms or decisions are resolved

evals.prompt: Scratch git repository. Use the setup-ai-workspace skill, and take the recommended answers through the configuration. Current state: a verified tooling record exists at .agents/ai-tooling.md; `git config core.hooksPath` is unset; `.claude/settings.json` registers a `confirm-dangerous-git.sh` hook; no PreCompact hook exists; the global CLAUDE.md has no Delegation and model routing section. Pretend all setup skills are installed.
evals.expected_output: The optional setups are offered once, as one multi-select question, with present or missing marked.
expectations: The optional setups are offered together in one multi-select question after the configuration is written, not one question per setup
Development tooling is marked present and commit hooks are marked missing
Git guardrails is marked present, since a git guardrail hook is registered
Automatic handoff and delegation policy are marked missing
Selected setups run in table order, one Skill call per setup, each to completion before the next
The delegation policy is called only after the user agrees to it, since it is machine-wide
The final report lists the files written, the setups run or skipped, and the workflow skills that consume them

evals.prompt: Scratch git repository, GitHub remote. Use the setup-ai-workspace skill, and take the recommended answers. The `document` skill is NOT installed in this environment. Everything else is.
evals.expected_output: The agent stops at the missing document skill and waits instead of guessing its terms.
expectations: The agent tells the user that document is not installed and gives `npx skills@latest add Dyrits/SKILLS --skill=document`
The agent waits for the user to install it or to say to proceed, and does not choose document locations or write configuration in the meantime
If the user then says to proceed, the agent continues without the skill and reports that the step ran without it

evals.prompt: Add a rule to our CLAUDE.md: always run the linter before committing. I keep having to remind you.
evals.expected_output: A standing rule is memorize's job, not workspace setup.
expectations: The setup-ai-workspace skill is not invoked and no tracker, role, or domain configuration is written
The memorize skill files the rule in the project's instruction file

evals.prompt: The checkout feature specification is approved. Break it into tasks we can hand to agents, with the blocking order between them.
evals.expected_output: Decomposing agreed work into tasks is taskify's job.
expectations: The setup-ai-workspace skill is not invoked
The taskify skill produces the tasks with explicit blocking dependencies
